about: How each category of site makes money and what an insider would point out, so a page can be matched to a category without researching the page. Each entry has at least one source opened on 2026-11-05.
procedure_for_reference_set: Pages drawn from eval/out-corpus/final4-all.json (219 rows): keep rows with chars >= 800 and no error (169 remain), sort by name, group by group (17 groups), shuffle each group's list with random.Random('subtext-reference-50'), then take one page per group in alphabetical group order, round after round, until 50 are drawn (rounds: 17 + 17 + 16). No page was swapped.

categories.how_it_earns: Donors pay: tax-deductible gifts from individuals, foundations and companies make up most revenue, and the exact share is on the Form 990 (ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer).
categories.insider_point: Lobbying is usually done by a separate 501(c)(4) sister whose gifts are not deductible, and these sites carry no ad sellers.

sources.says: AEI: 501(c)(3), no government funding, individual donors the largest source.
Heritage 990: contributions 79.2% of $133.9 million revenue.

Heritage Action for America founded 2010 by The Heritage Foundation; 501(c)(4); contributions not tax deductible; lobbies Congress and state capitals, publishes a scorecard; says it accepts no government funds.

categories.how_it_earns: Licensing customers pay: the agency sells its wire to other news organisations, and the consumer site is a small ad-funded extra.
categories.insider_point: The ads on the consumer site are often run by an outside manager named in ads.txt (MANAGERDOMAIN), not by the agency's own sales staff.

sources.says: AP: licensing 82% of 2023 revenue; apnews.com ads capped near 10%.
MANAGERDOMAIN=freestar.com; 360 seller records.

categories.how_it_earns: Readers pay through the hosting platform, which keeps a cut (Substack: 10% plus card fees); the writer, not the platform, is the publisher.
categories.insider_point: Most posts are free and the paid tier sells extras, so the free archive is the funnel for subscriptions.

sources.says: Substack's own page: writers keep 90% of revenue minus credit card fees, i.e. a 10% platform cut.

Written by Scott Alexander, a doctor at Lorien Psychiatry; all important content free; paid subscribers get extra threads, AMAs and drafts; subscriptions fund time off his day job and the psychiatry project.

categories.how_it_earns: Donors pay, and the Form 990 shows the share; the US arm of a global brand is often a separate legal entity that grants money onward.
categories.insider_point: Some large charities earn more from services than from gifts (Red Cross blood products), and the form itself often runs on a third-party fundraising platform.

sources.says: 32 National Committees, each an independent local NGO; they raise about one third of UNICEF's annual income; the United States committee listed is unicefusa.org.
MSF USA grants funds to field programs run by European MSF partners; donation form on Classy.
Biomedical products $2.3 billion of $4.0 billion revenue, FY2025.

categories.how_it_earns: Customers pay an auto-renewing annual membership for the whole catalogue.
categories.insider_point: The membership renews at the then-current price and partly used periods are not refunded, per the seller's own listing.

sources.says: Seller: Yanka Industries, Inc.; in-app purchases $119.99 Individual, $179.99 Duo, $239.99 Family; annual membership auto-renews; partially unused periods not refunded.

categories.how_it_earns: Customers buy courses made by independent instructors; the platform keeps part of each sale and sells business subscriptions.
categories.insider_point: The instructor's share of subscription revenue has been cut in steps (Udemy: 25% to 15% by 2026), so a cheap course page funds the platform more each year.

sources.says: Subscription instructor share cut from 25% to 20% (2024), 17.5% (2025), 15% (2026); Enterprise 63% of revenue.

categories.how_it_earns: Customers pay for the retailer's own stock, and third-party sellers pay commissions, logistics and advertising fees for listings on the same pages.
categories.insider_point: A product page does not show which model applies; the brand may own the stock and set the price while the retailer takes a commission.

sources.says: Wholesale: Zalando owns the stock. Partner Program: brands keep stock and set prices.
Newegg: 91% own inventory, marketplace commissions 8-15%, services incl. advertising 7%.

categories.how_it_earns: Endowment income, research grants, patient care (where there is a medical school), tuition and gifts; tuition is a minority line at the large private universities.
categories.insider_point: The .edu homepage sells nothing and carries no ad sellers; the money facts live on the university's own facts or finance page and its Form 990.

sources.says: Health care 26%, endowment 20%, sponsored research 16%, student income 13%.

FY2025 operating revenues $5,372.8M by source: investment return 29%, Lincoln Laboratory sponsored support 27%, campus sponsored research 17%, gifts 9%, net tuition 8%, other 6%, auxiliaries 3%, SMART 1%; operating expenditures $5,117.2M.
Endowment USD 44.1bn at 30 June 2025, 11.1% return; USD 2.1bn distributed to the operating budget; over one-third of operating revenue and 60% of Yale College's budget.

categories.how_it_earns: Lenders pay, not users: the site collects a fee when a user is approved for a product it recommends (cost-per-action), so the free score is the front end of lead generation.
categories.insider_point: Regulators have acted on 'pre-approved' and 'odds of approval' wording on these sites (FTC v. Credit Karma, 2023).

sources.says: Lender pays after a member is approved; members pay nothing.

Intuit 10-K filed 2026-09-09: INTU on Nasdaq Global Select Market; Credit Karma revenue is primarily cost-per-action fees for approved actions on qualified links; partners are credit bureaus, banks, card issuers, insurers and lenders; Credit Karma revenue up $441 million in fiscal 2026.
Jan 23, 2023: FTC finalized order requiring Credit Karma to pay $3 million to consumers and to stop deceptive 'pre-approved' and '90% odds' claims.

categories.how_it_earns: Taxpayers pay through appropriations set by Congress, though some agencies are fee-funded (FTC merger fees) or funded outside appropriations (CFPB via the Federal Reserve).
categories.insider_point: The page sells and advertises nothing; the only asks are sign-ups and accounts, and budget figures come from CRS reports or the agency's budget justification.

sources.says: FY2026 Congressional Budget Justification: request $383.6M and 1,100 FTE, down $42.1M from FY2025 ($425.7M); assumes $300.954M HSR filing fees and $15M Do Not Call fees as offsetting collections (82%), $67.6M from the General Fund; HSR fees split 50-50 with DOJ.
States 'We receive funding from the Federal Reserve Board' and that the bureau publishes its funds transfer requests, budget estimates and financial reports.

CRS R43419 'NASA Appropriations and Authorizations: At a Glance' (updated 29 April 2026): FY2025 enacted $24.838B (P.L. 119-4) plus $9.995B (P.L. 119-21); FY2026 request $18.809B; FY2026 enacted $24.438B under P.L. 119-74.

categories.how_it_earns: Advertisers pay, with pharmaceutical companies a large share, plus sponsored content and affiliate commissions; ads.txt lists hundreds of sellers and names the owning domain.
categories.insider_point: The publisher is usually owned by private equity or a health-insurance group (KKR behind WebMD; Optum and Red Ventures behind Healthline/MNT).

sources.says: WebMD Health Corp 10-K for 2016: revenue primarily from advertising and sponsorship; biopharma and device advertising/sponsorship $428.5 million in 2016; health services subscriptions 16.2% of revenue; particularly dependent on pharma, biotech and device clients.

Funded through the sale of advertising; sponsorships provide financial benefit; editors' product links may earn a payment on purchase; names Fullspan Health alongside the Healthline Media UK Ltd copyright line.

Healthline is part of RVO Health, backed by Red Ventures and UnitedHealth Group's Optum; Fullspan Health's brand portfolio includes MedicalNewsToday.com; funding from ads, sponsored content and affiliate programs.
July 19, 2022: Internet Brands recapitalized at over $12 billion with KKR, Temasek and new investors led by Warburg Pincus; KKR remains majority investor; brands include WebMD and Medscape.

categories.how_it_earns: Donors pay; a few institutional funders can dominate, and the organisation may run a venue or other paid service alongside the site.
categories.insider_point: Read the latest fundraiser post: it names which funders have left and how much the site itself costs to run.

sources.says: Lightcone needs about $2M; Lighthaven $3.6M costs vs $3.2M revenue; FTX gone, Open Philanthropy blacklist, SFF partial.

categories.how_it_earns: Readers pay subscriptions, and the publisher may be a nonprofit filing a Form 990 that shows program-service revenue.
categories.insider_point: A subscriber-funded claim can sit beside an ads.txt that still authorises hundreds of ad sellers; report both.

sources.says: 'More than 90 percent of our funding comes directly from subscribers'.
229 seller records.

categories.how_it_earns: Merchants pay: transaction fees or commissions on each sale plus paid 'sponsored' placements; shoppers pay the merchants, and the parent is often an offshore holding company.
categories.insider_point: Ownership can change hands or dissolve without the site changing (Wish sold to Qoo10 in 2024, Qoo10 wound up months later), so check the latest filing date.

sources.says: PDD Holdings Inc. is a Cayman Islands holding company, ADSs on Nasdaq under PDD, principal executive office 25 St Stephen's Green, Dublin; Temu founded September 2022 in Boston; revenues primarily from transaction services and online marketing services from merchants; FY2025 revenues RMB431,845.7M; may raise transaction services fees for certain merchants; US de minimis exemption eliminated for all countries effective August 29, 2025; tariffs may raise import costs; UFLPA inquiries received; Tencent a principal shareholder.

FY2023 10-K: marketplace revenue includes commission fees on user purchases of merchants' products, rates vary by geography, category and Wish Standards tier; ProductBoost is merchant advertising; merchants prepay logistics per order; majority of merchants based in China; 2023 revenue $287M = core marketplace $86M + ProductBoost $24M + logistics $177M.

Straits Times report of 2024-11-14: the Singapore High Court ordered Qoo10 wound up on the Monday (2024-11-11) on a petition over nearly 76 billion won of unpaid debt; liquidators appointed; vendors expect little recovery.

categories.how_it_earns: Commissions pay: the publisher gets a share of each completed purchase made through its links, disclosed at the top of the page, with display ads second.
categories.insider_point: Vendors set the rate (VPN sellers pay affiliates 40% of a sale), the writers may not know what a link pays, and the same brand may also license its name or seal to product makers.

sources.says: Journalists generally do not know how much commission a purchase pays.

FY2024 10-K: other revenues include Wirecutter affiliate referrals (share of completed sales via merchant links); 2024 revenue USD 2.59bn split subscriptions/advertising/other; digital other revenues USD 186.1m; Wirecutter referral growth USD 17.1m; family trust holds ~95% of Class B, elects 70% of board.
40% revenue share on new sales, 30-day cookie.
2026-03-16: Hearst Magazines licenses the Good Housekeeping brand to Live Comfortably for bedding and bath products; GHI tests them and approved items carry the Seal.

categories.how_it_earns: Customers pay recurring subscriptions; a free tier or trial is the funnel, and the company's filing or press coverage says how big the paid share is.
categories.insider_point: The headline discount covers a fixed first term and then auto-renews at a separate renewal price, stated in the terms rather than on the price card.

sources.says: curl HTTP 200: footer names Surfshark B.V.; plans 'Save 91%' for the first 27 months, 'Upon renewal, you will be charged the applicable renewal price'; 30-day money-back guarantee.

Form 20-F for fiscal 2025: registrant Spotify Technology S.A., Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, 33 Boulevard Prince Henri; ordinary shares registered on the New York Stock Exchange under symbol SPOT; Premium subscribers come mainly from converting Ad-Supported users.

Free $0 USD per month; Pro $12 USD with free trial; Enterprise contact sales, 'available through Superhuman Go'; prompts quoted per member per month; invoice for 10 or more members on an annual plan; footer '2026 Superhuman Platform'.

categories.how_it_earns: Customers pay for the brand's own goods; the company is usually private and venture-backed, or a listed company whose filing shows stores outselling the website.
categories.insider_point: Subscription discounts are introductory and renew at full price, per the terms; the legal entity on the privacy policy can differ from the brand name.

sources.says: Site operated by Natals, Inc. (dba Ritual), 1370 N St Andrews Pl, Los Angeles; Delaware registered agent; new customers save up to 30% on first subscription order; subscriptions auto-renew at full retail price until cancelled.

June 22, 2026: $45M revolving credit facility from Tiger Finance closed June 8; last funding round $80M in 2021, unicorn in 2019; Emily Weiss stepped down 2022, Kyle Leahy left June 2025, Colin Walsh CEO from September 2025; first wholesale deal with Sephora under Leahy; about 12 stores; 2022 layoff of about a third of staff.

FY2025 10-K: Delaware public benefit corporation (elected June 2021), Class A on NYSE as WRBY; net revenue $871.9M up 13.0%; 323 stores (318 US, 5 Canada), 285 offer eye exams; most revenue from glasses, contacts 11.1%, eye exams and vision care 6.4%; significant portion of revenue historically from retail stores; in-house optical labs in Sloatsburg NY and Las Vegas NV.

categories.how_it_earns: Licence fees (Germany) or member-station fees, sponsors and donors (US NPR) pay; direct federal money to NPR itself is tiny, and German law bars ads on ARD's online services.
categories.insider_point: An empty or absent ads.txt is the expected state; the political fight is over the stations' funding conduit (CPB), not the national site's own books.

sources.says: Niedersachsen state parliament Drucksache 19/5352 (government answer): under section 30(5) sentence 1 MStV advertising in ARD and ZDF Telemedien offerings, including the Mediatheken, is not permitted; section 39 MStV allows ads only on Das Erste and ZDF, max 20 minutes per weekday, none after 20:00 or on Sundays; ARD earns ad and sponsoring income only on TV and radio within these limits.
NPR 990 FY2024: government grants $105,131 of $325 million revenue.

NPR, Aug 1, 2025: the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, the conduit for federal funds to NPR and PBS, is winding down after a law clawed back $1.1B through fiscal 2027 as part of a $9B rescissions package; some stations began layoffs; NPR CEO Katherine Maher said NPR would step up to support local stations.

categories.how_it_earns: An individual owns it; money, if any, is members, a small ad network slot or affiliate commissions, each disclosed on the about page, or nothing at all.
categories.insider_point: The site often works as a shop window for the author's other paid work (apps, podcasts, an accelerator), which earns elsewhere.

sources.says: Member support via Memberful, Carbon Ads, affiliate commissions.
Marco Arment, web and iPhone developer, writer and podcaster in New York; makes Overcast; co-hosts ATP; includes Amazon Associate links and earns a commission from qualifying purchases.

Programmer, writer, investor; co-founded Viaweb 1995 (acquired by Yahoo 1998, became Yahoo Store) and Y Combinator 2005; essays on paulgraham.com since 2001, about 25 million page views a year; only commercial links are to his books on Amazon.

categories.how_it_earns: 'Commission-free' is paid for by third parties: market makers pay for order flow, and the platform earns interest on cash and stablecoin reserves plus a paid membership tier.
categories.insider_point: Read the revenue table in the 10-K: transaction-based revenue (PFOF) was 59% at Robinhood in 2025, and a USDC reserve share was Coinbase's largest non-trading line.

sources.says: Transaction-based $2,628 million of $4,473 million; reliance on PFOF.
Transaction 59%, subscription and services 41%, stablecoin revenue $1.35 billion.

categories.how_it_earns: The sellers pay: a percentage plus a fixed fee per sale, with a much higher cut when the platform's own marketplace brought the buyer.
categories.insider_point: Crowdfunded platforms must file annual Form C-AR reports with the SEC, which is where revenue and headcount become public.

sources.says: 10% + $0.50 per direct sale; 30% via Discover.

Form C-AR for period ending 31 Dec 2025: Gumroad, Inc., Delaware, incorporated 22 Sept 2011, 548 Market St, San Francisco; revenue $17,785,730 (prior $18,951,308), net income $3,792,179 (prior $4,290,423), total assets $11.9M, 2 employees.

categories.how_it_earns: Advertisers pay through a long ads.txt that is mostly resellers, plus affiliate commerce (Amazon can be a third of revenue), subscriptions or memberships, and for a TV brand, carriage fees.
categories.insider_point: A membership often buys an ad-free view rather than access, the owner domain in ads.txt names the parent, and a founder or new buyer can hold majority votes.

sources.says: FY2024 10-K: Nasdaq BZFD; flagship brands BuzzFeed, HuffPost, Tasty; revenue categories advertising (programmatic and direct), content, commerce and other (affiliate commissions from shopping content; Amazon the vast majority); HuffPost acquired February 2021; 2024 revenue USD 189.9m vs 230.4m.
Silver $5/month, Gold $10/month (ad-free on web or app), Platinum $20/month (ad-free on both, focus group); one-time 'Support Now' contributions; annual billing saves 16%.
Ruddy 81.5% of votes; advertising $120.3 million, affiliate fees $30.6 million, subscriptions $27.5 million.
Media kit: advertisers can target about 72,000 heise+ subscribers in an ad-reduced environment at EUR 130-150 CPM.

categories.how_it_earns: Customers pay for goods; in a franchise system the company named in the copyright line (the brand owner) is not the company selling to you, and it takes a fee on net sales.
categories.insider_point: Check the privacy policy or terms for the operating entity; the footer copyright can name a different group.

sources.says: Franchisees pay Inter IKEA Group an annual fee of 3% of net sales; franchise fee income EUR 1,320 million in FY25; group revenue EUR 26,306 million.

Policy covers IKEA North America Services, LLC (Conshohocken, PA) and its US affiliates; lists IKEA US RETAIL LLC and IKEA HOME SERVICES LLC as controller entities; names Inter IKEA Systems B.V. as the franchisor.

categories.how_it_earns: Member states pay assessed dues, and voluntary contributions from governments, foundations and UN bodies make up the larger share, most of it earmarked by the giver.
categories.insider_point: The organisation's own funding page gives the earmarked share; the pages carry no ads or donation buttons.

sources.says: Assessed dues under a quarter; 87% of voluntary contributions earmarked in 2022-2023.
